title: Get preflight through tower-http CorsLayer
summary: CorsLayer and TraceLayer go in, Any plus allow_credentials panics at startup, so the origins are named and listed.

turns.user: frontend on localhost:5173 dies on CORS. we have tower-http now, add CorsLayer. auth is cookies so it sends credentials: 'include'. also want access logs, TraceLayer

assistant.body: Great setup! CorsLayer answers the preflight and TraceLayer opens a span per request. A Content-Type of application/json is not one of the headers CORS treats as safe, so allow_headers names it. Cookies are sent, so allow_credentials(true) goes on as well. TraceLayer writes at DEBUG, so the subscriber has to allow DEBUG or you will see nothing.

turns.user:
panics the moment it starts
Invalid CORS configuration: Cannot combine `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. Any and allow_credentials(true) cannot be combined. A browser refuses Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on a request with credentials, so tower-http panics while building the layer to tell you early. In other words, if cookies are allowed, origins have to be named. Replacing Any with an explicit HeaderValue.

sed -i '' -e 's/use axum::http::{header, Method};/use axum::http::{header, HeaderValue, Method};/' -e 's/use tower_http::cors::{Any, CorsLayer};/use tower_http::cors::CorsLayer;/' -e 's|\.allow_origin(Any)|.allow_origin(HeaderValue::from_static("http://localhost:5173"))|' src/main.rs

Sure. allow_origin also takes an array of HeaderValue, so both go in. Only a matching origin is echoed back, and CorsLayer adds Vary: origin itself. Any origin not on the list gets no allow header, and the browser blocks it.
